conclusion: The image returns normally and CPU0 loaded-wake median improves as predicted, from histogram upper endpoint 127.958 to 122.625 us. Performance acceptance fails: the observed maximum increases from 160.542 to 197.333 us. The worst wake contains 88.417 us inside the remaining CPU0 tick handler and 108.917 us after it returns. Its exit class and switch work are absent from version-1 per-wake data, so the regression remains unexplained and blocks landing. The 50.5 us maximum slow IRQ exit instead occurs between the idle and busy phases, with 23.583 us of expiry work. Whole-run masking falls to 68.042 us and the task-lock maximum is 16.083 us. Further board runs are held for diagnosis.

conclusion: The software checks preserve both event-progress obligations while removing the redundant event from records with no post-unlock lifetime work. No board timing improvement or complete masked-span bound is established.
narrative: The checker runs the existing concurrent publication, off-CPU suspend and transfer, late publisher, retirement and nested FIFO gate cases. The added deterministic observer case requires the first record release to signal before the next FIFO wait and the retirement callback to precede its completion signal. Its two independent omitted-event variants fail the named assertions. The first unlock-negative compilation exposes an unused fixture parameter; the corrected fixture reruns only the failed negative steps, and both reject. The event observer models software ordering, not hardware timing or a full ARM memory model. Independent review approves the conditional and the progress checks. The frozen correlated board diagnostic predates this optimization and retains the unconditional final event.
